questions.q: In Temporal, how does work reach your code?
options: The Temporal server calls your service over HTTP
Your worker polls a task queue and pulls the work
Your client runs the workflow code directly
questions.why: Temporal is pull-based: workers poll task queues. Restate is push-based: the server calls your service.

questions.q: A customer starts a workflow and 'nothing happens': status Running, no errors. What's the first thing to check?
options: Whether any worker is polling that task queue (and namespace)
Whether the workflow id is unique
questions.why: With no poller, work waits silently on the queue. `temporal task-queue describe` shows pollers.

questions.q: Where should a call to a payment API go in Temporal?
questions.why: Side effects live in activities. Workflow code must stay deterministic, and the TypeScript sandbox blocks direct I/O.

questions.q: Why do Temporal workflows import activities with `import type`?
options: Workflow code runs in a sandbox and must not load activity code; it only needs names and signatures
questions.why: The workflow schedules activities by name through proxyActivities; the worker runs the actual activity code outside the sandbox.

questions.q: What is Temporal's default activity retry policy?
options: Unlimited attempts with exponential backoff (1s, doubling, capped at 100s)
Retry until the workflow times out, then pause
questions.why: Unless maximumAttempts is set, activities retry forever with backoff.

questions.q: An activity throws ApplicationFailure.nonRetryable('Card declined'). The workflow doesn't catch it. What happens?
questions.why: Non-retryable failures skip retries and surface as ActivityFailure in the workflow; unhandled, the workflow fails.

questions.q: Workflow code (not an activity) throws a TypeError because of a bug. What happens?
options: The workflow task fails and is retried; the workflow stays Running until a fix is deployed
Temporal restarts the workflow from the beginning
questions.why: Only Temporal failure types (like ApplicationFailure) fail a workflow. Other errors are treated as bugs: the workflow task is retried so work isn't lost.

questions.q: Which message kind lets a client change a workflow's state AND get a result back?
questions.why: Signals are fire-and-forget, queries are read-only, updates do both.

questions.q: Restate has virtual objects for per-entity state. What's the usual Temporal equivalent?
options: A long-running entity workflow per entity, changed by signals/updates and read by queries
questions.why: One workflow per entity (e.g. workflow id cart-dana) processes its messages one at a time, much like a virtual object.

questions.q: A cart workflow has been receiving signals for months. Why might it need continue-as-new?
options: Its event history keeps growing; histories have size limits and long ones replay slowly
To move it to another namespace
questions.why: Continue-as-new starts a fresh run with the same id and an empty history, carrying state forward.

questions.q: In Temporal's TypeScript SDK, is `Math.random()` safe inside workflow code?
options: Yes: the sandbox replaces it with a deterministic, seeded version
questions.why: The sandbox makes Math.random and Date replay-safe. Code changes under running workflows are a separate problem.

questions.q: After a deploy, some running workflows fail their workflow tasks with a non-determinism error. What's the best first move?
options: Roll back the deploy, then reintroduce the change behind patched() or Worker Versioning
questions.why: Rolling back lets stuck workflows replay on compatible code. Then make the change safely and add replay tests.

options: Check, offline, whether new workflow code can replay a saved real history without non-determinism
Copy a workflow to another namespace
questions.why: Replay tests catch breaking changes before they reach production.
